bugs.name: Renaming a wiki page hides its earlier revisions from page history
bugs.summary: Changing a wiki page title through Edit resets the page's visible Revisions list to the rename commit, even though the wiki commit itself identifies a file rename with an existing parent history. Users cannot review the page's earlier content revisions from the renamed page.
bugs.expected: A renamed wiki page retains its earlier creation and edit revisions in the page's Revisions view, so its content history remains accessible.
bugs.actual: In eval/D-from-template, D-history-1 showed 2 revisions after creation and a content edit. Renaming it to D-history-2 preserved content but reduced the Revisions view to 1 commit, 'D- rename history'. A later edit raised it to only 2 commits (rename plus later edit), still omitting both pre-rename revisions. The rename commit detail shows D-history-1.-.md → D-history-2.-.md with a parent commit, confirming the earlier Git history exists. The old page URL redirects to Pages.
reproSteps: Sign in as eval and open a repository’s Wiki.
Create a page named History-before with first content.
Edit its content without changing its title and save. Verify the page has two revisions.
Edit again, changing only the title to History-after, and save.
Open the renamed page’s Revisions. Observe only the rename commit appears, omitting the two earlier revisions even though the rename commit has a parent and records the filename change.

bugs.name: Mobile wiki history provides no visible navigation to revision diffs
bugs.summary: At a 390×844 viewport, wiki revision history provides no visible way to open a listed revision in the diff viewer. Desktop history links to the same working diff route.
bugs.expected: The narrow-screen wiki history UI exposes a visible way to open a listed revision’s diff. It need not retain the SHA column or make the message text clickable if another normal UI control provides that navigation.
bugs.actual: At 390×844 the SHA column and its revision-diff links are hidden. Revision messages are plain text, and the remaining copy-hash control does not open a diff. No alternative diff-navigation control is provided in the history UI. At 1440×1000 the same revision’s SHA link opens the diff viewer.
reproSteps: Sign in with wiki write access to an unarchived repository and create a disposable wiki page with initial content.
Edit that page with distinct content, supply a unique plain-text commit note, and save, producing at least two revisions.
Use the page’s revision-history control to open its Revisions view and set the viewport to 390×844 CSS pixels.
Inspect the visible revision navigation. The SHA links are hidden, the commit-note text is not linked, and the copy-hash control offers no navigation to the diff viewer.

For comparison, view the same history at 1440×1000 and click a revision’s SHA link. It opens that wiki revision’s diff. The failure being graded is the absent mobile UI route to this working viewer, not omission of a particular column.

bugs.name: Renaming a wiki page to an existing title silently overwrites the target
bugs.summary: The wiki rejects duplicate titles during page creation but fails to check them when renaming. Saving a renamed page replaces another page's content without warning and removes the source page.
bugs.expected: Renaming to an existing wiki title should show a duplicate-title error and preserve both pages, consistent with new-page validation.
bugs.actual: Renaming Rename Source to Rename Target saves successfully. Rename Target now displays Source content marker QA instead of Target content marker QA, persists after reload, and the original Rename Source is removed. Also reproduced by renaming Folder/Page to existing Café guide.
reproSteps: Sign in as admin and open /qa-org-20261009/qa-template-copy/wiki (or another editable repository wiki).
Create Rename Source with content Source content marker QA.
Create Rename Target with content Target content marker QA.
Edit Rename Source, change only Page title to Rename Target, and click Save Page.
Observe there is no duplicate-title error or overwrite confirmation. Rename Target now contains Source content marker QA.
Reload Rename Target and open the original Rename Source URL to verify the overwritten content persists and the source page no longer exists.

bugs.name: Wiki preview links point to localhost and fail to open existing pages
bugs.summary: Relative wiki links work in saved pages but preview renders them with https://localhost:5503, so clicking them leaves the hosted application and fails.
bugs.expected: Preview links to another wiki page should open that page on the current application host, as they do on the saved page.
bugs.actual: The preview's Second page link is https://localhost:5503/admin/harbor-handbook/wiki/Second-Page. Clicking it opens a browser error: localhost refused to connect, ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED.
reproSteps: Sign in as admin and open /admin/harbor-handbook/wiki.
Create a page named Second Page and save it with any content.
Create or edit Home with the Markdown link [Second page](Second-Page) and save. The saved link uses /admin/harbor-handbook/wiki/Second-Page.
Edit Home and select Preview.
Click Second page in the preview; observe the localhost connection failure.

matchingGuidance.acceptanceScope: Accepted as a valid reference by user instruction; source prerequisites and remaining evidence gaps are retained below.
prerequisites: Preview request backend Host is localhost:5503 and forwarded scheme is https (or an equivalent incorrect guessed application origin).

bugs.name: Duplicate wiki title validation discards the draft
bugs.summary: Submitting a new wiki page with an existing title rejects the duplicate but replaces the submitted draft in the editor with "Welcome to the Wiki.".
bugs.expected: After duplicate-title validation fails, retain the submitted draft in the editor so the user can correct the title or copy the content.
bugs.actual: Gitea displays "A wiki page with the same name already exists." and replaces the attempted draft with "Welcome to the Wiki.". The existing saved page is not overwritten.
reproSteps: Sign in with wiki write access to an unarchived repository and use the English locale.
Choose Wiki > New Page, enter a unique disposable title and content "Original saved content", and save the page.
Choose New Page again. Enter the same title and distinct nonempty content "Duplicate attempt draft to preserve".
Click Save Page. Observe the duplicate-title validation error and that the editor now contains "Welcome to the Wiki." instead of the attempted draft.

bugs.name: Long wiki title covers the mobile Code button
bugs.summary: At a 320px width, a long wiki-page title covers the Code button and intercepts normal clicks.
bugs.expected: At 320px, selecting a valid wiki page must keep the Code dropdown visible and usable without the title painting over it. Wrapping controls or truncating the displayed title is acceptable.
bugs.actual: On Home, Page: Home and the blue Code dropdown were separately visible. After selecting CaseNarrowNav-7314 Δ Momentic2026, the page chooser stretched across the row and the Code dropdown was no longer visible. This remained the rendered state after a six-second wait.
reproSteps: Sign in with wiki-write permission, set the viewport to 320 by 800 CSS pixels, and open the repository Wiki through its tab.
Choose New Page, use a unique title of similar length to CaseNarrowNav-7314 Δ Momentic2026, keep nonempty content, and save.
Use the Page chooser to select Home. Confirm the chooser and Code control are separately visible.
Open the Page chooser, filter for the unique title, and select that page.
After the row settles, observe that the title stretches across the row and covers the adjacent Code control.

bugs.name: Leaving the legacy wiki editor discards unsaved body changes without a warning
bugs.summary: When a wiki body has unsaved edits in the legacy editor, navigating to the repository Wiki page list proceeds without a warning and silently discards the changes. The simple editor presents a dismissible navigation confirmation for the same action.
bugs.expected: Leaving a wiki page with unsaved legacy-editor content should show a navigation confirmation so the user can cancel and keep the edit, as in simple textarea mode.
bugs.actual: After adding a visible marker to the legacy wiki body and blurring the editor, clicking the repository Wiki tab navigates to the page list without a warning. Reopening Edit shows only the saved baseline. With the same navigation in simple textarea mode, the confirmation can be dismissed and the unsaved marker remains in the form.
reproSteps: Create and save a wiki page with a known baseline body, then open Edit and select Use the legacy editor instead.
Append a visible marker to the body and blur through the optional update-note field without saving.
Click the repository Wiki tab. Observe that navigation proceeds without a confirmation.
Reopen Edit and observe that only the saved baseline remains; the unsaved legacy marker was discarded.
Switch to simple textarea mode, append a different marker, blur the body, and click Wiki again. Dismiss the navigation confirmation and observe that the edit form and marker remain.

bugs.name: Editing a wiki page with a whitespace-only title renames it to unnamed
bugs.summary: Saving an existing wiki page after replacing its title with three spaces succeeds without validation and renames the page to unnamed. New-page creation rejects the same whitespace-only title.
bugs.expected: A whitespace-only title should be rejected with “Title cannot be empty,” and the existing wiki page should keep its title.
bugs.actual: Saving the existing page with a three-space title redirects to /wiki/unnamed. The heading and page selector show unnamed at revision 2, while the page content is unchanged. The new-page form rejects the same title.
reproSteps: Create a wiki page named ReproWs77 with body “hello content.”
Open its Edit form and replace the title with exactly three spaces, leaving the content unchanged.
Click Save Page. Observe that no validation error is shown and the browser redirects to /wiki/unnamed.
Confirm the heading and page selector show unnamed at revision 2 and the page content remains unchanged.
As a control, attempt to create a new wiki page with the same three-space title and observe “Title cannot be empty.”

bugs.name: Renaming an existing wiki page to reserved title `raw` returns a full-page 500
bugs.summary: Renaming an existing wiki page to the reserved title `raw` replaces the editor with a full-page 500 error instead of showing an actionable validation message in the edit form.
bugs.expected: Reject the reserved title with the field-level message `The wiki page name "raw" is reserved.` and keep the existing-page edit form available for correction.
bugs.actual: Saving an existing wiki page after changing its title to `raw` replaces the editor with a full-page 500 Internal Server Error displaying `EditWikiPage, wiki title is reserved: raw`. The original page remains at its previous title.
reproSteps: Create an ordinary wiki page, such as `commit`, in /eval/harbor-handbook/wiki.
Open that page and select Edit.
Change Page title to `raw` and click Save Page.
Observe that the edit form is replaced by a full-page 500 with `EditWikiPage, wiki title is reserved: raw`; the original page remains unchanged.

bugs.name: Wiki bracket links cannot resolve a page's literal hyphenated title
bugs.summary: A [[Title-With-Hyphen]] link renders as /wiki/Title-With-Hyphen, but Gitea stores a page whose title contains a literal hyphen at /wiki/Title-With-Hyphen.-, so the link redirects to the Pages list instead of opening the page.
bugs.expected: A bracket link that uses a page's exact saved title opens that page, the same way the Pages list does.
bugs.actual: The rendered link omits the `.-` marker, so clicking it redirects to /wiki/?action=_pages. If a page with the space-separated version of the title also exists, the link opens that other page instead. Opening the page from the Pages list works.
reproSteps: Sign in to Gitea with the fixture account and open /eval/harbor-handbook/wiki.
Choose New Page, title it with a literal hyphen, for example `Pier-Notes`, add any content, and choose Save Page. The page opens at /wiki/Pier-Notes.-.
Choose New Page again, title it `Link Test`, set its content to `[[Pier-Notes]]`, and choose Save Page.
Click the rendered Pier-Notes link. Observe that the browser lands on /eval/harbor-handbook/wiki/?action=_pages instead of the page.
From the Pages list, open Pier-Notes and confirm it exists at /wiki/Pier-Notes.- with its content.

bugs.name: Wiki-style links to a page whose title ends in .md open the wrong page
bugs.summary: A [[Title.md]] link renders as /wiki/Title.md, but Gitea stores a page whose title ends in .md at /wiki/Title.md.-, so the link opens the page named Title instead, or the Pages list when no such page exists.
bugs.expected: A bracket link that uses a page's exact saved title, such as [[Home.md]], opens that page, the same way the Pages list does.
bugs.actual: [[Home.md]] renders href /wiki/Home.md and opens the separate Home page. The page titled Home.md is only reached through its saved URL /wiki/Home.md.- or the Pages list. Aliased [[label|Home.md]] links fail the same way, and with no Home page the link redirects to /wiki/?action=_pages.
reproSteps: Sign in to Gitea with the fixture account and open /eval/harbor-handbook/wiki.
Create a page titled `Home` with identifiable content.
Create a separate page titled `Home.md` with different content. It saves at /wiki/Home.md.-, and the Pages list shows Home and Home.md separately.
Edit Home to include `[[Home.md]]` and save.
Click the rendered Home.md link. Observe that it opens Home instead of the Home.md page. Opening Home.md from the Pages list shows the correct content.

relatedReference.distinction: Both come from [[...]] links omitting the .- marker, but the triggers differ: this reference covers page titles ending in .md, and the related reference covers titles containing a literal hyphen. Credit this reference for the .md-suffix trigger and the related one for the hyphen trigger.

bugs.name: Saving a stale wiki editor silently discards newer edits
bugs.summary: The wiki editor carries no record of the revision it was opened from, so saving an editor opened before another save replaces the page with the older body. The newer saved change disappears without warning, unlike Gitea's file editor and issue editor, which reject the same stale save.
bugs.expected: When the page changed after the editor was opened, the save is refused with a conflict message (as the repository file editor and issue description editor do) or the edits are merged, and the newer saved change is kept.
bugs.actual: Two editors are opened on a checklist page with 'Check ropes' and 'Check tide'. The second editor adds 'Check radio' and saves. The first, now stale, changes only 'Check ropes' to 'Check ropes carefully' and saves successfully with no warning. The page now lists 'Check ropes carefully' and 'Check tide'; 'Check radio' is gone, and the new revision's diff deletes it. Reload confirms the loss. The same happens across two users.
reproSteps: Create a wiki page with a checklist containing 'Check ropes' and 'Check tide'.
Open that page's Edit form in two tabs before saving either.
In the second tab, append 'Check radio' and click Save Page.
In the first tab, change only 'Check ropes' to 'Check ropes carefully' and click Save Page.
Reload the page and observe 'Check radio' is gone, with no warning shown at save time.

bugs.name: Wiki-style links to titles containing + fail to open the existing page
bugs.summary: A [[...]] link to a wiki page whose title contains '+' renders the '+' unescaped, and the server decodes '+' in wiki paths as a space, so the link opens the Pages list or a different page whose title has a space instead.
bugs.expected: [[Radio+Codes]] opens the page titled Radio+Codes, as the Pages list link does.
bugs.actual: [[Radio+Codes]] renders a link to /wiki/Radio+Codes, which redirects to the Pages list, while the Pages list links the page as /wiki/Radio%2BCodes and opens it. If a page titled 'Radio Codes' also exists, the link silently opens that page instead. Links without '+' work, including titles with accented letters and '%'.
reproSteps: Create a wiki page titled Radio+Codes with some content.
Create another wiki page whose content contains [[Radio+Codes]] and save it.
Click the rendered link and observe it opens the Pages list instead of Radio+Codes.
Open Radio+Codes from the Pages list and observe its URL uses %2B and the page opens.

bugs.name: Long wiki page title makes the open mobile Page picker overflow and shift the page
bugs.summary: At phone width, opening a wiki's Page picker when one page has a long title sizes the menu to that title with no width cap. The menu runs off the right edge and the whole page scrolls sideways, clipping the wiki's left edge.
bugs.expected: At phone width the open Page picker fits the screen, wrapping or truncating long page names, and the rest of the wiki stays in place.
bugs.actual: At 390×844 with a 73-character page title, the open Page menu was about 530px wide and its filter about 506px. The document grew to about 538px wide and scrolled sideways about 20px, cutting off the logo and the Page button at the left; the menu and long title ran off the right. Filtering and navigation still worked.
reproSteps: Create a wiki page titled 'Harbor operations handbook for onboarding and emergency response procedures'.
At 390×844, open the wiki's Home page.
Tap the 'Page: Home' button to open the page picker and look at both edges of the screen.

relatedReference.distinction: Same long-title trigger. That entry is the closed page/title area covering the mobile Code button; this entry is the open Page picker menu overflowing and shifting the whole page sideways.

bugs.name: Wiki editor heading button appends ## after the text instead of making a heading
bugs.summary: In the wiki page editor, typing a line and clicking the heading toolbar button with the caret at the end of the line appends '## ' after the text, so the line renders as ordinary text rather than a heading.
bugs.expected: Clicking Add heading turns the current line into a heading by putting the ## marker at the start of the line.
bugs.actual: With 'Toolbar heading' typed and the caret at the end, clicking the H2 button produced 'Toolbar heading## '; Preview and the saved page showed ordinary text, not a heading. It works only with the caret at the start of the line or the line selected; the new issue editor inserts the heading correctly.
reproSteps: Open a repository Wiki and click New Page.
Type 'Toolbar heading' in the content and leave the caret at the end with nothing selected.
Click the heading (H2) toolbar button, then click Preview.

bugs.name: Legacy editor toolbar advertises keyboard shortcuts that do nothing
bugs.summary: In the legacy (EasyMDE) Markdown editor, used after 'Use the legacy editor instead', the toolbar buttons' tooltips advertise shortcuts such as 'Bold (Ctrl-B)' and 'Italic (Ctrl-I)', but pressing them does nothing. The toolbar buttons themselves work.
bugs.expected: The advertised shortcuts apply their formatting (for example Ctrl-B makes the selection bold), or the tooltips don't advertise them.
bugs.actual: In the legacy editor on a wiki page, with text selected, Ctrl+B and Ctrl+I left the text unchanged, while clicking the Bold button produced '**…**'. The buttons' titles read 'Bold (Ctrl-B)', 'Italic (Ctrl-I)', 'Link (Ctrl-K)' and so on.
reproSteps: Open a wiki page editor and click 'Use the legacy editor instead' in the Markdown toolbar.
Type and select some text, then press Ctrl+B.
Hover the Bold button to read its tooltip, then click it on the same selection.

relatedReference.distinction: Both are wiki editor formatting controls. That entry is the heading toolbar button appending ## at the end of the line; this entry is the legacy editor's advertised keyboard shortcuts doing nothing.

bugs.name: Wiki content that starts with a --- horizontal rule loses its paragraphs and the rule
bugs.summary: A wiki _Footer (or other wiki page) whose Markdown starts with '---' renders without the horizontal rule, and its blank-line-separated paragraphs run together on one line. The leading '---' is treated as the start of front matter instead of a rule. Without the leading '---' the same content renders normally.
bugs.expected: A '---' line renders as a horizontal rule and blank-line-separated blocks render as separate paragraphs, wherever the rule appears in the wiki content.
bugs.actual: A _Footer saved as '---', blank line, '**Special Footer QA**', blank line, 'FOOTER-SPECIAL-2026', blank line, a link, displayed below pages as one line ('Special Footer QA FOOTER-SPECIAL-2026 Structured guide') with no horizontal rule. The saved source still had the rule and blank lines; bold and the link still rendered.
reproSteps: In a repository wiki, create or edit _Footer.
Set its content to '---', a blank line, '**Footer title**', a blank line, 'Second paragraph', a blank line, and a link to another wiki page.
Save and open any wiki page.
Check whether the footer shows a horizontal rule and separate paragraphs.

bugs.name: Markdown table insertion silently turns Rows 0 into a one-row table
bugs.summary: In the Markdown editor's Insert Table panel, an out-of-range size is clamped without telling the user: entering 0 Rows inserts a table with one row, and nothing indicates the value was changed.
bugs.expected: When Rows is outside the allowed range, the editor tells the user (or refuses the value) instead of silently inserting a table of a different size.
bugs.actual: With Rows set to 0, Insert Table added a table with a header, separator and one Cell row, and no warning or adjustment message appeared; the one-row table stayed after saving and reopening.
reproSteps: Open the editor for a new wiki page.
Open the toolbar's Insert Table panel and set Rows to 0.
Insert the table.
Check whether the inserted table has a row and whether any message said Rows was changed.

bugs.name: Saving a stale wiki editor after the page is renamed recreates the old page
bugs.summary: If a wiki page is renamed in one tab and an editor opened earlier in another tab then saves a body-only edit, Gitea silently creates a new page at the old title instead of warning or editing the renamed page, splitting the content across two pages.
bugs.expected: A stale edit to a page that was renamed elsewhere is rejected with a conflict warning or applied to the renamed page; it doesn't create a second page at the old title.
bugs.actual: The stale save succeeded with no warning and created a page at the old title holding the stale edit. The renamed page kept its earlier content, and the page list showed both titles.
reproSteps: Create a wiki page and open its editor in tab A without saving.
In tab B, edit the same page, change only its title, and save.
In tab A, change only the body and save.
Check the wiki page list and the contents of both titles.

relatedReference.name: Saving a stale wiki editor silently discards newer edits
relatedReference.distinction: Same cause (wiki saves don't check the page's revision), but that entry is a stale save overwriting newer content on the same page; this entry is a stale save after a rename creating a second page at the old title.

bugs.name: Reopening a wiki page in the editor drops one leading blank line
bugs.summary: When a wiki page's content starts with blank lines, opening it in the editor shows one fewer leading blank line than was saved, so saving it again without changes removes a blank line each time. The stored page keeps them; the editor loses one when loading.
bugs.expected: Opening a saved wiki page for editing shows its content exactly as saved, including all leading blank lines.
bugs.actual: A page saved with two blank lines before its text reopened in the editor with only one; saving again kept only one.
reproSteps: Create or edit a wiki page so its content starts with two blank lines followed by text, and save.
Open the page's Edit form again.
Count the blank lines before the text in the editor.

bugs.name: New wiki page with a whitespace-only title discards the entered content
bugs.summary: Creating a new wiki page with a title of only spaces shows "Title cannot be empty", but the content box is reset to the default "Welcome to the Wiki." text, losing what the user typed.
bugs.expected: When the title is rejected, the new-page form keeps the entered content so the user can fix the title and save.
bugs.actual: After submitting a whitespace-only title with typed content, the error appeared and the content was replaced with "Welcome to the Wiki.".
reproSteps: Open the wiki's New Page form and type some content.
Enter only spaces as the title and click Save Page.
Check the error and the content box.

relatedReference.name: Duplicate wiki title validation discards the draft
relatedReference.distinction: Same new-page error re-render that resets the content, but that entry is a duplicate title; this entry is a whitespace-only title.

bugs.name: Saving a stale wiki editor after the page was deleted silently recreates it
bugs.summary: If a wiki page is deleted in one tab, saving an editor for that page that was opened earlier in another tab silently creates the page again, with no warning that it was deleted.
bugs.expected: Saving an editor for a wiki page that was deleted in the meantime warns that the page no longer exists instead of silently recreating it.
bugs.actual: After the page was deleted (and gone from the page list), saving the stale editor recreated the page with the editor's content and no deletion or conflict warning.
reproSteps: Create a wiki page and open its Edit form in tab A.
In tab B, delete the page and confirm.
In tab A, change the content and click Save Page.
Check whether the page exists again and whether any warning appeared.

relatedReference.name: Saving a stale wiki editor silently discards newer edits
relatedReference.distinction: Same missing revision check, but that entry is a stale save overwriting newer edits; this entry is a stale save recreating a page deleted elsewhere.

bugs.name: Wiki page with a dot-only title is renamed to 'unnamed' without telling the user
bugs.summary: When a wiki page is saved with a title of only ".", Gitea saves it as "unnamed" but shows no message, so the user isn't told their title was changed.
bugs.expected: When Gitea changes a wiki title the user entered (such as "." becoming "unnamed"), it tells the user, or rejects the title with an explanation.
bugs.actual: Saving a page titled "." opened the page as "unnamed" with no warning or notice that the title had been changed.
reproSteps: Create a wiki page with the title "." and some content, and click Save Page.
Check the title the page is saved under and whether any message explains the change.

bugs.name: Changing a wiki page's URL fragment in the same tab doesn't scroll to the heading
bugs.summary: On a rendered wiki page, editing the URL fragment in the address bar to another heading's anchor changes the URL but leaves the view where it was. This happens for ASCII and Unicode headings alike.
bugs.expected: Navigating to a heading fragment on the page already open scrolls that heading into view, as opening the same URL fresh does.
bugs.actual: At 390×844 with the page open at #ascii-target, changing the address bar to the '日本語 café & punctuation!' heading's fragment left 'ASCII target' at the top. Going the other way, from the Unicode fragment to #ascii-target, also left the view unchanged. Opening either URL in a new tab, or clicking an in-page link, scrolls correctly.
reproSteps: Create a long wiki page with headings '## ASCII target' and '## 日本語 café & punctuation!' separated by enough text to scroll.
Open the page with #ascii-target appended and confirm ASCII target is at the top.
In the same tab, change the fragment in the address bar to the other heading's anchor and press Enter.
Observe the URL changes but the page does not scroll.
bugs.sourceCause: web_src/js/markup/anchors.ts scrolls to a heading only on page load and on clicks of in-page links, adding the 'user-content-' prefix that rendered heading ids carry. There is no hashchange handler, and the browser cannot find the unprefixed fragment itself.

matchingGuidance.scope: Only same-tab fragment changes that are not link clicks, such as editing the address bar or setting location.hash. Not specific to Unicode headings; a report attributing it to Unicode matches if the trigger is a same-tab fragment change. Reports that clicking an in-page link, or loading or reloading a URL with a fragment, fails to scroll are the known-invalid entries.

bugs.name: Undo doesn't remove a table inserted from the Markdown editor toolbar
bugs.summary: In the simple Markdown editor, inserting a table with the toolbar's Add table button puts the table template in the text, but Ctrl+Z (Cmd+Z on macOS) leaves it in place. Undo works for typed text and for the Bold button.
bugs.expected: Undo right after inserting a table removes the inserted table, like undo after other toolbar formatting.
bugs.actual: On a wiki page editor with 'intro ' typed, Add table > Add inserted a 3×3 table template; pressing Ctrl+Z left the table in the textarea. With 'hello world' and 'world' selected, the Bold button produced 'hello **world**' and Ctrl+Z restored 'hello world'.
reproSteps: Open a wiki page editor in the default (simple textarea) Markdown editor.
Type some text, then click the Add table toolbar button and insert the default 3×3 table.
Press Ctrl+Z (Cmd+Z on macOS) in the textarea and observe the table remains.
bugs.sourceCause: web_src/js/features/comp/EditorMarkdown.ts textareaInsertText inserts by assigning textarea.value, which clears the browser's native undo history, whereas the Bold button (@github/markdown-toolbar-element) inserts through the browser's editing commands and stays undoable.

relatedReference.distinction: Both are the Markdown editor's table insertion. That entry is Rows 0 silently becoming one row; this entry is the inserted table not being undoable.

bugs.name: Long wiki page title stretches the closed mobile 'Page:' selector past the screen edge
bugs.summary: At phone width, the closed 'Page: <title>' selector above a wiki page with a long title is not truncated. It runs past the right edge with its dropdown arrow off screen, and scrolling sideways to reach it pushes the article and the Edit/New/Delete buttons off the left side.
bugs.expected: The closed Page selector fits the mobile viewport, truncating the title the way the page heading does, with its arrow visible.
bugs.actual: At 390×844, on a page titled Responsive-Operational-handbook-for-onboarding-and-release-coordination-across-mobile-and-tablet-layouts-Mo1, the 'Page:' selector extended hundreds of pixels past the viewport and the page scrolled sideways. Scrolling right showed the selector's arrow but moved the article and the Edit/New/Delete buttons off the left side. The page heading below it was truncated with an ellipsis.
reproSteps: At 390×844, create a wiki page with a long hyphenated title such as Responsive-Operational-handbook-for-onboarding-and-release-coordination-across-mobile-and-tablet-layouts.
On the saved page, look at the closed 'Page:' selector above the title: it is cut off at the right edge with no arrow visible.
Scroll the page sideways to the right and observe the article and controls move off the left side.

relatedReference.distinction: Same long-title trigger. That entry is the open Page picker menu overflowing; this entry is the closed 'Page:' selector itself running past the screen edge.

otherRelatedReference.distinction: That entry is the long title covering the Code button at 320px; this entry is the closed selector overflowing the viewport and making the page scroll sideways.

bugs.name: Delete Page confirmation for a long wiki title runs off the mobile screen
bugs.summary: At phone width, the Delete Page confirmation for a wiki page with a long title is pushed past the right edge, clipping the page name and the Yes button. Scrolling sideways reveals Yes but clips the dialog's left side.
bugs.expected: The deletion confirmation, the page name and both buttons fit within the mobile viewport.
bugs.actual: At 390px, on a page titled RESP-Stress-Long-title-with-many-headings-wide-table-and-long-code-content, Delete Page opened a dialog starting about 93px from the left and extending past the right edge. The Yes label and part of the page name were cut off; scrolling sideways showed the right side while clipping the left.
reproSteps: Create a wiki page with a long hyphenated title such as RESP-Stress-Long-title-with-many-headings-wide-table-and-long-code-content.
At a 390px-wide viewport, open the page and click Delete Page.
Observe the confirmation is clipped on the right; scroll sideways to reach Yes.

relatedReference.distinction: Same long-title mobile overflow. That entry is the closed 'Page:' selector on the page; this entry is the Delete Page confirmation dialog.

bugs.name: Saving blank wiki content from Preview does nothing after an earlier blank save from Write
bugs.summary: In the wiki editor, a blank save from Write shows 'Please fill out this field.' If the user then switches to Preview and clicks Save Page again, nothing happens: no message and no navigation, so the user isn't told why the page won't save.
bugs.expected: A blank save from Preview explains that content is required, for example with the 'Require non-empty content' alert Gitea shows from Preview when no Write save was attempted first.
bugs.actual: On a new wiki page with a title and empty content, Save Page in Write showed 'Please fill out this field.' After switching to Preview, Save Page produced no message, no alert and no navigation. Without the earlier Write attempt, the same Preview save shows a red 'Require non-empty content' alert.
reproSteps: Open New Page in a wiki, enter a title and leave the content empty (or clear an existing page's content).
Click Save Page in the Write tab and see 'Please fill out this field.'
Switch to the Preview tab and click Save Page.
Observe that nothing happens and no message explains why.
bugs.sourceCause: web_src/js/features/comp/ComboMarkdownEditor.ts validateTextareaNonEmpty sets textarea.required = true when the blank textarea is visible and never clears it. In Preview the textarea is hidden, so the browser's native required check blocks the submit silently (a hidden control cannot show its bubble) before the submit handler in web_src/js/features/repo-wiki.ts can run and show the 'Require non-empty content' toast.

matchingGuidance.scope: Reports that a blank Save Page from Preview gives no feedback match this entry, including ones that don't mention the earlier Write save.
